description: The kill-switch integration is broken and double-counted. (1) REQ-S5 (lines 252-254) calls `self-recover.sh <slot> survival-bankruptcy <net_usdc>` but the skeleton's Group J dispatcher has NO handler for reason 'survival-bankruptcy' (defined reasons are needs-login, spawn-surface-drift, hook-module-unrecognized, adversary-stalled, backoff-cap, token-kill-switch, token-source-degraded). The reason falls through to an undefined path. (2) REQ-S5 claims this 'in turn calls the skeleton's REQ-B4 kill-switch mechanism (writes loop.disabled)', but skeleton REQ-B4 (lines 219-234) is triggered INSIDE loop-roi.sh by the predicate cumulative_token_cost_jpy > 5*cumulative_jpy_earned — it is NOT reachable via self-recover.sh. The described bridge does not connect to any real mechanism. (3) Two contradictory kill CRITERIA now target the same loop.disabled file: skeleton REQ-B4 = cost_jpy > 5x earned_jpy, grace anchored to first_seen_ts; eval REQ-S5 = net_usdc < 0 (any loss), grace anchored to loss_start_ts. Different thresholds, different grace anchors, different currencies — a slot can be simultaneously 'alive' by one and 'bankrupt' by the other.

evidence.snippet: THE SYSTEM SHALL call self-recover.sh <slot> survival-bankruptcy <net_usdc> (skeleton REQ-F1) which in turn calls the skeleton's REQ-B4 kill-switch mechanism
